ModMetaData.name: Jawa Patches (local)
ModMetaData.author: mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
Local content + compatibility patches for the "crashed Factory ship / Jawa stowaways" gravship campaign. Self-authored, kept minimal and defensive. Each PATCH is wrapped in PatchOperationConditional so a missing target (mod not loaded, def renamed in an update) is a silent no-op instead of a red error. LOAD THIS LAST in the mod order (RimSort), after every mod it touches.
Currently contains: - Defs/WeatherDefs/SWDesertWeather.xml — four hazard weathers (sandstorm, dry sandstorm, red fog, red foggy rain) extracted from "Star Wars - Biomes Addon" (Ferreira312, WS 2298926362). Pure XML, no assembly: the mod's custom C# overlay classes were swapped for the vanilla fog overlay while keeping all gameplay fields (accuracy/move/wind/lightning). Sandstorm cuts ranged accuracy to 0.25; dry sandstorm adds lightning-started fires; red fog / foggy rain reduce accuracy (and, for the rain, move speed). - Patches/AnimalBiomeDuplicates_Fix.xml — removes 3 duplicate (biome, animal) registrations that crash BiomeDef.CommonalityOfAnimal(). Armadillo x AridShrubland and Armadillo x Desert (Beasts of the Rim's animal-side wildBiomes duplicating Odyssey's biome-side wildAnimals), and Titan x TropicalSwamp (the Titans mod lists the biome twice in its own def). Left unfixed these kill Choose Wild Animal Spawns outright, make Giddy-Up skip its animal-biome cache, and abort Biome Compatibility Project inside RimWorld's post-load queue. Detected by Utils/animal_inventory.py; re-run it after mod updates. Nothing is lost in-game — the biome-side registration still spawns the animal. - Patches/BiomeAnimalDanglingRefs_Fix.xml — the null-key sibling of the above. Primordial Geysers injects animals into its biome guarded on the mod name only, and five of the named PawnKindDefs do not exist here (Vanilla Animals Expanded drops badger/moose/muskox/porcupine when Odyssey is active, via IfModNotActive in its LoadFolders.xml; AA_WaywardMobileAssembler was removed from Alpha Animals). Each leaves a BiomeAnimalRecord with a null animal, and BiomeDef.CommonalityOfAnimal then throws ArgumentNullException on the null key — which is what kept Choose Wild Animal Spawns dead. Removing them costs nothing: they spawn nothing, and the biome already lists vanilla Porcupine and Moose. These nodes are created by another mod's patch at runtime, so they do not exist on disk and offline validators report zero matches; that is expected, and it is why this mod must load after Primordial Geysers. - Patches/SWCPZoomerIcon_Fix.xml — kills the last red error in the load. Star Wars KotOR Resources and Materials ships an AssetBundle reference it never packaged, so SWCP_VATS_Zoomer's custom Graphic_Zoomer returns a null Material and vanilla BuildableDef.ResolveIcon throws a NullReferenceException every launch. Verified from IL that exactly one def is responsible, and that BuildableDef's PostLoad lambda skips ResolveIcon entirely when uiIconPath is non-empty — so adding uiIconPath (512blank, a texture the mod already ships) makes the NRE structurally unreachable without changing any runtime behaviour. Note this is hygiene, not a rescue: the post-load queue does NOT abort on a failed action, contrary to what our notes long claimed. The two "Failed to load bundle" lines will remain; only the exception goes. - Patches/HeadSetForFA_Revive.xml — Head Set For [NL] Facial Animation has been dying in its static constructor every launch. Verified from IL: FaceAdjustmentDef's constructor never initialises AgeBasedParams, and CheckSettingData walks that list for any race with life stages. A sweep of all 45,525 XML files in the load set found exactly one adjustment def that omits the field — BS_InsectoidHumanoid_FourArmed_FaceAdjustment, created at runtime by Facial Animation Compatability Project. Adding an empty list fixes it. NOTE this is hygiene, not the appearance fix: HeadSetForFA only does head size/offset tuning and never touches eye nodes or head types. - Patches/DroidFemaleTexture_Fix.xml — Outer Rim Droid Depot ships only male body textures. All 11 droid body folders were checked and none has a Naked_Female variant, so any droid generated female renders with no body at all. Forces fixedGender Male on the 7 affected PawnKindDefs, which routes generation to textures that exist. Chose this over hasGenders=false because that yields Gender.None, whose Naked_None path does not exist either and would break every droid instead of some. - Defs/GeneDefs/JawaEyeColours.xml — adds Jawa_Eyes_HugeOrange and Jawa_Eyes_HugeAmber. Star Wars Xenotypes ships only two huge (Jawa-style) eye colours, yellow and red, which is thin for a whole colony. Cloned verbatim from guy762_Eyes_HugeYellow and re-tinted with <color> rather than new art, so they keep the exact glowing silhouette. Added to BTD_Jawa so the engine rolls between yellow, orange and amber per pawn. The abstract parent GeneEyeColor carries the exclusion tag EyeColor, so eye-colour genes are mutually exclusive and listing several on one xenotype makes RimWorld pick one; guy762_xenotype_hutt already relies on this with four colours. They stay individually assignable in Character Editor for the five authored founding Jawa. Do NOT edit a non-human pawn's head in Character Editor — it destroys the head (confirmed on Mon Calamari and Bith). - Patches/JawaAppearance_Tuning.xml — three appearance decisions. (a) Biotech's Skin_InkBlack is actually (55,55,55) charcoal; set to true (0,0,0). Note this is a Core gene shared by 13 active xenotypes, not Jawa-only. (b) Removes Outland_GreaterGoblinoidHead from BTD_Jawa: that head's ART has arachnid eyes and fangs baked in, which drew underneath the yellow-eye gene and gave Jawa two sets of eyes plus a fanged mouth. Without it the face is plain and only the glowing eyes show, which is the canonical read. (c) Adds Outland_AllMale so Jawa spawn male-only this playthrough. - Patches/SWDesertWeather_Attach.xml — injects those weathers into hot/arid biomes (sandstorms) and volcanic/exotic biomes (red fog) via baseWeatherCommonalities. Conditional-wrapped per biome. Tune the commonality numbers there to taste. - Defs/QuestScriptDefs/Jawa_TheClaim.xml — "The Claim", the campaign's first authored quest. Something came down past the ridge; clan law says the wreck belongs to whoever plants a marker on it first, and someone else is already walking. It is an item-stash site on the ground layer, offered on the ordinary opportunity cadence, expiring after 10–18 days with no penalty and no goodwill loss — the only thing lost is the opportunity. The haul is fixed rather than rolled so the reward rule is guaranteed instead of hoped for: one advanced component (the one category a starting clan cannot make, needing advanced fabrication and a fabrication bench), eight industrial components and four steel slag chunks. Deliberately at the low end. No node class, field or defName in it is guessed — each was read off a shipping def (Core's Script_ItemStash and Script_BanditCamp, Royalty's Script_Intro_Deserter and Scripts_Permits) and the file cites the path and line for every one. DLC defs are named for PROVENANCE only and never depended on: everything the quest actually references ships in Core, so a DLC or mod update cannot orphan it. everAcceptableInSpace is set true, and that field gates ACCEPTANCE BY THE PLAYER, not site placement — proven twice, from Core's keyed string QuestNotSpace ("cannot accept in space") sitting inside the run of quest accept-requirement strings, and from Odyssey's six genuinely orbital site quests setting the field zero times while Core's ground-only trade request sets it true. Core's own item-stash quest omits it, which means vanilla's stash quest is silently unacceptable while the colony is aboard a ship; this is a gravship campaign, so ours sets it and the site still lands on the ground. The rival clan that beats you to the wreck is a STORY FACT — no FactionDef is authored or referenced by it, and it exists only to explain why there is a timer. - Defs/ThingDefs_Items/Jawa_ClaimRumour.xml — "salvage rumour", a one-use readable that hands the player The Claim on the spot rather than waiting for the storyteller to offer it. Three comps do the entire job: CompProperties_Usable, CompProperties_UseEffectDestroySelf and CompProperties_UseEffectGiveQuest. Those comps are mostly USED by Biotech defs but the classes live in Assembly-CSharp, so this needs no DLC and references no DLC def. The pattern is borrowed rather than invented — Space Tower's ST_TowerMap is a shipping example of exactly this three-comp readable, and it was read before this was written. Note that the defName is Jawa_ClaimRumour while the label is "salvage rumour": that mismatch is deliberate, because a defName is never shown to the player and renaming it would churn the quest reference and every save holding one for no player-facing gain. This ships as the bare object — tradeability None, no faction, no price. Where rumours come from is designed and is NOT built here: bought from the Hutt Cartel, who know where everything fell and will sell you anything, AND found in wreck loot, because a clan that cannot afford rumours must never simply stop receiving content. Both lanes, trader stock and loot tables, are one line each and are the next step, not this one. To see it now: Debug actions, Spawn thing, Jawa_ClaimRumour; then select a colonist and right-click the item to read it. - Defs/TerrainDefs/JawaSaltCrust.xml — adds Jawa_SaltCrust, a hard pale evaporite pan: flat, blinding, takes footprints like chalk, grows nothing, and is the firmest ground on the planet. It is COSMETIC ONLY and that is a design guardrail, not an omission — fertility 0, no yield, no comp, nothing farmable or harvestable, because farmable-anywhere or passive-resource terrain is an anti-exponential violation dressed as scenery. Salt as a trade good is a separate, later piece of work. The art is reused, not drawn: texturePath is Odyssey's own Terrain/Surfaces/DryLakeBed, which nothing in Core, any DLC or any biome def actually references — it ships unused, so this terrain adopts it rather than competing with it. The consequence worth knowing is that the texture lives in Odyssey's asset bundle, so the crust's appearance depends on Odyssey being active. <color> pushes the cracked hardpan toward evaporite white; if a future version stops honouring colour on natural terrain, DryLakeBed is still visually distinct from Sand and SoftSand, so this degrades to "less white" rather than to "invisible" — which is why it beat tinting Sand. ParentName is NaturalTerrainBase and NOT Sand on purpose: inheriting from Sand would also inherit its tools (kick material in eyes) and its sand filth, neither of which belongs on a mineral crust. Every remaining field was copied from a def read on disk, with the source file and line recorded per field. - Patches/JawaTerrain_SaltPans.xml — the attachment half of the above. A TerrainDef on its own generates NOWHERE, exactly as a WeatherDef on its own blows nowhere; a biome has to ask for it, and this file is that ask. It adds a terrain patch maker for Jawa_SaltCrust to the three CORE arid biomes — Desert, Extreme Desert and Arid Shrubland — tuned to read as one big lake bed rather than a speckle: perlin frequency below Core's, a minimum patch size roughly double Core's, and a fertility ceiling so pans only form on the driest ground. What the player sees is broad, pale, cracked salt pans lying in the low ground of desert maps, unmistakably not sand and flat enough to build and land on. Desert and Extreme Desert already own a terrainPatchMakers node so those are a plain conditional add; Arid Shrubland has no such node at all, so it is guarded on the CONTAINER and the nomatch branch creates the whole element — adding a child to a node that does not exist is the failure mode where one dead operation silently kills every operation after it in the same sequence. The sibling dune file guards Arid Shrubland identically, so whichever applies first creates the node and the other takes the match branch: order-independent by construction. One thing NOT to hunt: Geological Landforms Harmony-patches TerrainPatchMaker itself, and on a tile carrying a landform that landform's own graph can write terrain over the biome result. On ordinary tiles the pans generate normally. Geological Landforms' own dry-lake landform hard-codes soft sand and sand, so the one map feature that ought to be a salt pan is the one place this cannot reach. - Patches/JawaTerrain_DuneSeas.xml — turns the arid maps from a flat sheet of sand with occasional soft patches into a dune sea. It adds NO new def and NO new art: Core already ships one SoftSand patch maker per hot desert biome, and the only number touched is that threshold's lower bound — 0.65 down to 0.55 in Desert and to 0.50 in Extreme Desert, because the deep desert is the dune sea proper and is already 100 percent sand at every fertility. Lower threshold means more of the perlin field clears the bar, which means wider dunes; perlin output clusters around 0.5, so 0.65 is roughly the top sixth of a map and 0.55 roughly the top third. Arid Shrubland has no dunes at all today and gains one patch maker, kept off the fertile ground so the biome still reads as shrubland rather than as a second desert. This is the one terrain change with a gameplay cost rather than a purely visual one: SoftSand is path cost 14 against Sand's 4, so widening the dunes genuinely slows a crossing, and that is intended — the world is a desert sea to cross, not a place to settle. Those two numbers plus Arid Shrubland's are the entire tuning surface; raise them back toward 0.65 to undo. The replace operations select on the SoftSand threshold specifically, which is what keeps them order-independent against the salt-pan file adding a second entry to the same list. - Defs/MapGeneration/JawaScrapfields.xml plus Patches/JawaResource_Scrapfields.xml — the pair that strews the desert with wreckage. The first declares a GenStepDef that scatters steel slag chunks with machine-bit filth trodden around them; the second registers it into the player map generator, because a GenStepDef that no MapGeneratorDef lists runs on no map at all. What the player sees is slag lying half-buried across the open desert — not in ruins, not in a mountain, out where you land — so the planet reads as somewhere things have been crashing for a very long time, which is the reason a clan of scavengers is standing on it. Slag was chosen because it is the cheapest possible thing to strew: it smelts to 15 steel and only after a smelter, power and hauling, so a littered map is atmosphere with a work cost attached rather than free loot. Raising the vanilla junk-cluster density instead would have handed out sealed crates of finished gear, which is an arms race this campaign does not want. Every field on the gen step is copied from a shipping GenStep_ScatterThings; clusterSize and spotMustBeStandable were deliberately left out because they appear on no shipped def of that class anywhere, and a field the engine does not read is a silent no-op at best. The one number worth arguing about is the count: 12–20 per 10,000 cells puts roughly 75 to 125 chunks on a 250x250 map, two or three visible per screen, which is the density that makes the world READ as junk-strewn — Core's own debris step runs 0.25–0.5, one or two per map. Full theoretical yield if every chunk were smelted is about 1,100 to 1,900 steel per map, one-off and non-renewing. It is registered against the player-settlement generator ONLY, deliberately, so encounter maps, faction bases and quest maps are untouched; one more operation aimed at the abstract common generator widens it to the whole planet.
⚠️ The two terrain patches and the scrapfields scatter all act at MAP GENERATION TIME. None of them changes a map that already exists — the salt pans, the wider dunes and the slag fields appear on newly generated maps only.
